text.text_excerpt: Cafe Abyssinia was my first time with Ethiopian food! Stopped by on a whim and could not be happier that I did! The waiter was so helpful and answered questions about what the dishes were and didn't mind that we didn't know anything about it, he was happy to share. He said that his favorite dish was the kitfo which is equivalent to beef tartare, but they also will cook the meat to be rare or well-done (tried well done since it was the first time trying it). Also tried the Doro Wat, which is apparently Ethiopia's national dish and for good reason! It's chicken cooked in this really rich, thick stew/sauce of tomatoes, onions, and really good spices. These two dishes came out on one large pl...

Being my first Ethiopian outing, I was surprised how familiar the food was while the dining methods ended up relatively unorthodox. Every bit of it was a lot of fun, though. Between two of us, there was more than enough portions of each item ordered, and the staff was friendly. I wish I could go into more detail, but my visit was about a year ago. I do remember the food generally being on the spicy side, so that's a plus if you're into that. I'm not, but my girlfriend loved it. Aside from that aspect, I found everything well-prepared and quite good. The lamb in particular had a really great flavor. I'm long overdue for another visit, and it's certainly happening in the near future.

5 stars?! Yes. 5 stars because as far as Ethiopian food goes, this is one of the best places I have ever been to. With a friendly staff to boot. I suppose I am a lil biased as I LOVE LOVE LOVE ethnic food and the minute (almost literally!!) I saw this ethiopian gem in Edible New Orleans I rushed over there. First off, I should say my ethiopian experience is limited to Boston and LA. I don't really know how "authentic" ethiopian is supposed to taste like but I will judge based on the quality of the dishes. My bf and I started with the beet salad. I hate beets. I do!
